title: Selective Safety Steering via Value-Filtered Decoding
claim: Our thresholded policy intervenes only when needed, with error that stays low across value distributions, unlike the smooth baseline.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right, shared legend at right, distribution formulas below
description: Three side-by-side line plots share the same axes: error bound eta from 0 to 0.5 on the x-axis and max TV distance from 0 to 1 on the y-axis. Each plot shows a solid blue staircase curve for the proposed policy. Three dashed red curves in different shades show the Gibbs baseline at lambda = 2, 5 and 10. Light gray vertical lines mark the token values' distances from the threshold c. A legend sits to the right of the plots. Captions below each plot give the setting and its value distribution: (a) polarized, far from c; (b) uniform spread, U(0,1); (c) concentrated near c, Normal(c, 0.03^2). In (a) the blue curve stays at zero until about 0.4, then steps up. In (b) it rises in even steps. In (c) it jumps to 1 almost immediately. The eye goes first to the blue staircase against the smooth red curves.
caption: Worst-case TV distance (lower is better) for our policy $\pi_c$ (solid) and the Gibbs policy $\pi_g$ (dashed) under three token-value distributions with $c=0.5$. Gray vertical lines mark each token’s absolute distance from the threshold $c$. From left to right: $V_t$ values far from $c$, $V_t$ values uniformly distributed on $(0,1)$, and $V_t$ values concentrated near $c$.
abstract: While large language models (LLMs) are trained to align with human values, their generations may still violate safety constraints. A growing line of work addresses this problem by modifying the model's sampling policy at decoding time using a safety score. However, existing decoding-time steering methods often intervene unnecessarily, modifying generations that would have been safe under the base model. Such unnecessary interventions are undesirable, as they can distort key properties of the base model such as helpfulness, fluency, style, and coherence. We propose a new test-time steering method designed to reduce such unnecessary interventions while improving the safety of responses. Our approach filters tokens using a value-based safety criterion and provides an explicit bound on the probability of false interventions. A single threshold hyperparameter controls this bound, allowing practitioners to trade off higher rates of unnecessary intervention for better output safety. Across multiple datasets and experiments, we show that our value-filtered decoding method outperforms existing baselines, achieving better trade-offs between safety, helpfulness, and similarity to the base model.
